alt: The elements of an array above the Fenwick tree built from them. One tree position at a time is filled in. The block of elements it covers is marked on the elements, and that block always ends at the position and is as long as the position's lowest set bit.

steps.caption: 8 elements sit in positions 1 to 8. The tree below them starts unfilled. Each tree position will hold the sum of a block of elements that ends at that position.
Position 1 is 0001 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 1, so tree[1] covers just position 1. The sum is 3.
Position 2 is 0010 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 2, so tree[2] covers 2 elements ending at 2: positions 1 to 2. The sum is 5.
Position 3 is 0011 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 1, so tree[3] covers just position 3. The sum is 1.
Position 4 is 0100 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 4, so tree[4] covers 4 elements ending at 4: positions 1 to 4. The sum is 10.
Position 5 is 0101 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 1, so tree[5] covers just position 5. The sum is 5.
Position 6 is 0110 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 2, so tree[6] covers 2 elements ending at 6: positions 5 to 6. The sum is 6.
Position 7 is 0111 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 1, so tree[7] covers just position 7. The sum is 2.
Position 8 is 1000 in binary. Its lowest set bit is 8, so tree[8] covers 8 elements ending at 8: positions 1 to 8. The sum is 21.
The tree is full. A position with a higher lowest set bit covers a longer block, so most positions hold short blocks and only a few hold long ones.
